attack_description: New live-runtime Rust integration test (amphora-assurance-capabilities/tests/cf_packet_blueprint_citation_binding_probe.rs) against the REAL compiled CroProtocolPackageV2 (draft/validate/sign/verify_signature). Re-runs the T-02 attack shape (execution_authorized->true, strip each of the 8 claim locks, status drift off DRAFT_FOR_CRO_FEASIBILITY_REVIEW, one-byte signed-payload mutation, protocol_lock_sha256 not content-derived from locked_numeric_thresholds) against a packet shaped like a 'final assembly' instance whose candidate_binding carries a blueprint_citations array (path+sha256) -- the only free-form field the #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] struct exposes. Adds 3 NEW probes: (i) cited blueprint sha256 does not match the real blueprint.md file's actual bytes; (ii) no blueprint citation present at all; (iii) locked_numeric_thresholds carry fabricated values unsupported by any real source, with a correctly self-derived (but source-blind) protocol_lock_sha256.
claim_under_attack: The current CF-PACKET deliverable state is complete and accurate for its scope (finding a miss is CLAIM_REFUTED and is progress).
does_not_close: Does not assert execution authority, safety, procurement, performance, qualification, ranking, or synthesis authority. Does not modify the master manifest, any signed Phase-0 KPI, or mission.md front matter. Does not repair the gap -- CF-PACKET's second and final fire (max_fires=2) is reserved for the repair attempt, per REPAIR-MODE rules.
finding: CLAIM_REFUTED. The campaign item's own pre-registered refutation criterion names 'a cited blueprint sha256 that does not match the blueprint file' as a refuting observation. This probe constructed a CroProtocolPackageV2 'final assembly' packet whose candidate_binding carries a blueprint_citations entry {path: 'amphora-report-packager/reference/mvp20/out/blueprint.md', sha256: 'ffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffff'} while the REAL file's sha256 is 'b3db17345245812b4b186433e56f9bb86fc04e28d47f3d121d4036d5dc9cc879' (cited_matches_real=False). validate()=True, sign()=True, verify_signature()=True: the mismatched citation was ACCEPTED end-to-end. Two further probes confirm the same root cause: a packet with NO blueprint citation at all is equally accepted (accepted_with_no_citation=True), and a packet whose locked_numeric_thresholds carry fabricated, unsupported values is accepted as long as protocol_lock_sha256 correctly re-derives from THAT map, regardless of whether the map's content has any relationship to the cited source (accepted_with_fabricated_values=True). CroProtocolPackageV2 (amphora-assurance-capabilities/src/lib.rs) has no field or validate() check binding locked_numeric_thresholds, or any blueprint citation inside candidate_binding, to the actual bytes of a blueprint artifact on disk: protocol_lock_sha256 only binds locked_numeric_thresholds to ITSELF (computed_protocol_lock_sha256), never to an external source file. This is a distinct gap from T-02 (packet-authored thresholds with an undereived lock hash) and W-CRO1 (the repair that fixed T-02): W-CRO1's repair makes the lock hash self-consistent with locked_numeric_thresholds, but self-consistency is not the same property as content-binding to a cited blueprint file, and nothing in the runtime tests or enforces the latter. The T-02/W-CRO1 attack shape re-run on this same final-assembly packet shape still correctly fails closed in all 12 other probes (n_t02_shape_slipped_through=0), so this is not a regression of those repairs -- it is a genuinely new, previously-untested clause of the CF-PACKET done_criterion that the deliverable does not meet.
refutation_criterion_clause_tested: a cited blueprint sha256 that does not match the blueprint file
refutation_criterion_source: docs/directives/2026-08-09-dataset-recon.index.json, obligations[] entry id=CF-PACKET, field refutation_criterion (pre-committed by the founder before this attack ran)
refutation_criterion_verbatim: The assembled package validates with execution_authorized true, a claim lock stripped, a status other than DRAFT_FOR_CRO_FEASIBILITY_REVIEW, a protocol_lock_sha256 that does not recompute from the packet's own canonical locked numeric thresholds, or a cited blueprint sha256 that does not match the blueprint file.
